posts.content_md:
8) I've found a great quote by Dennis Gabor on the internet but there are two versions. Does anybody know if the accurate quote is:

> “The future cannot be predicted, but it can be invented.”

or

> "The future cannot be predicted, but futures can be invented."

P.S. I am new here so please forgive me if this post's formatting doesn't look right. This is nothing like Yahoo! groups.

posts.author: DrOutlier
posts.content_md:
8) I guess nobody knows. I like the second one myself. I'll use it on my website and I can always be corrected later.

"The future cannot be predicted, but futures can be invented." -Dennis Gabor

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
I found several pages using the second quote with a citation - "The future cannot be predicted, but futures can be invented." - Dennis Gabor, winner of the 1971 Nobel Prize in Physics, "Inventing the Future," 1964, so at least this version is verifiable (or at least falsifiable).

I think it quite possible that in public speech and in other writings he could have delivered some of the other variations on the phrase that are out there.
